name: Place Mohammed V
hero_subtitle: The civic heart of Casablanca, framed by imposing Art Deco and neo-Mauresque public buildings.

overview.title: Downtown’s Architectural Showcase
overview.p1: Place Mohammed V is the ceremonial and administrative core of central Casablanca. Around it stand the wilaya (prefecture), the law courts, the post office and other public buildings that mix Art Deco lines with neo-Mauresque detail — a signature of the Protectorate-era city plan.
overview.p2: It is not a place you linger for hours, but it is essential if you care about 20th-century architecture. The square and its fountains work well as a starting point for a walking tour of the downtown grid.
overview.p3: Combine it with the nearby Villa des Arts, the Marché Central or a tram ride toward the Corniche. Early morning or late afternoon light is best for photographs of the façades.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Place Mohammed V

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Central and well connected by tram and taxi. Easy walking distance from many downtown hotels.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Daytime for open views of the façades; late afternoon for softer light.

3.title: Photography
3.desc: The buildings are the main subject — early or late light works best.

q1.question: Is Place Mohammed V free?
q1.answer: Yes. The square and exterior views of the buildings are public.

q2.question: How long should I spend?
q2.answer: Thirty to sixty minutes is enough for most visitors.

q3.question: Can I go inside the buildings?
q3.answer: Most are working government buildings and not open as tourist sites. Enjoy the exteriors.

q4.question: What should I combine it with?
q4.answer: Villa des Arts, Marché Central, or a tram toward the Corniche.

q5.question: Why is it important?
q5.answer: It is the clearest expression of Casablanca’s 20th-century civic and Art Deco identity.
